problem_text: Can MVFA's few-shot fusion be made inductive — scoring each image on its own, without the test-set min-max normalisation of the released code — without losing AUROC, and does this give a threshold that transfers to unseen modalities? The inductive fusion standardises each branch with leave-one-out statistics of the K normal support images (each support's zero-shot map, and its few-shot map against a memory bank built from the other K-1 supports, pooled over patches and levels), adds the standardised branches, and pools the fused map with the mean of its top 2% pixels; the threshold is the 95th percentile of the supports' leave-one-out image scores. Primary outcome: image- and pixel-level AUROC of inductive versus transductive fusion on every held-out modality and K in {2, 4, 8, 16}. Motivating measurement: the spread of the transductive AUROC across random test subsets and at 10% and 50% prevalence. Secondary outcomes: sensitivity, realised specificity, F1 and expected calibration error at the support-derived threshold. We also record whether the few-shot baselines compared in the target paper (APRIL-GAN, WinCLIP) normalise over the test set in their public code, to judge how widely the finding applies.

ranking.title: Harmonic-mean p-value fusion with region-mass scoring: per-image MVFA scores that stay valid under dependent levels

Novelty.review: Combining layer-wise p-values, including dependence-robust rules, has been used for DNN input anomaly detection (arXiv 2007.15147); using support-anchored p-values to replace MVFA's verified transductive fusion is the new element.

Feasibility.review: Inference-only changes to the scoring code; trivial compute.

Clarity.review: Clear statistic, pooling and thresholds; the correlation analysis is a good addition.

Impact.review: Delivers deployable per-image scores with a statistically grounded threshold, fixing two verified defects.

Validity.review: The harmonic mean p-value is approximately valid under dependence; empirical p-values are discrete at small K, which limits resolution at very low levels.

ranking.title: Brown-corrected Fisher fusion: dependence-adjusted p-value combination estimated from support normals, with region-mass pooling

Novelty.review: Empirical Brown's method and layer-wise p-value combination exist; the combination with support-anchored nulls for MVFA is new in application.

Clarity.review: Clear formulas for scale and degrees of freedom.

Impact.review: Could keep Fisher's power with corrected validity.

Validity.review: Moment matching from strongly spatially correlated pixels of very few supports may be unstable at K = 2, and Brown's approximation can be poor in the far tail.

ranking.title: Empirical p-value fusion across levels and branches (Fisher-MVFA)

Novelty.review: Fisher combination of empirical p-values is standard (and used for layer-wise DNN anomaly detection); application to MVFA's fusion is the new part.

Impact.review: Fixes the transductive fusion with an interpretable statistic.

Validity.review: Fisher assumes independent p-values; MVFA's levels and branches are strongly dependent, so the statistic is anti-conservative — a flaw later evolution addressed.

ranking.title: LOO-Z inductive fusion with region-mass image scoring and a single support-derived operating point

Novelty.review: Normalising anomaly scores with held-out normal statistics is standard practice in tooling such as Anomalib, and leave-one-out calibration of anomaly detectors exists; the contribution is applying it to MVFA, not a new technique.

Feasibility.review: Inference-only with a small new module.

Clarity.review: Exceptionally clear: statistics, clipping, weights, pooling, thresholds and stability analyses are fully specified.

Impact.review: Directly removes both verified scoring defects and quantifies how much published few-shot numbers depend on test-set composition.

Validity.review: Sound and assumption-light; Gaussian z-scores are a rough tail approximation but adequate for ranking.

ranking.title: FDR-controlled anomaly maps: Benjamini-Yekutieli discoveries per image from support-anchored pixel p-values

Novelty.review: Conformal and FDR-controlled segmentation with guarantees exist (industrial defects 2504.17721; medical instance segmentation 2504.04482); the per-image BY procedure on support-anchored p-values for MVFA is an adaptation.

Feasibility.review: Inference-only; BY on 289 patches is trivial.

Clarity.review: Clear q levels, statistics and evaluation.

Impact.review: Gives the anomaly map a clinically meaningful guarantee on flagged regions.

Validity.review: Patch p-values come from a pooled support null across positions, so exchangeability between support and test patches at different anatomical positions is questionable; BY may be conservative for small lesions.

ranking.family: Learned calibration from source episodes or synthetic data

Novelty.review: Episodic few-shot adaptation exists in other anomaly detection domains (audio), but learning p-value weights from simulated source-modality episodes for medical VLM detectors was not found.

Feasibility.review: Requires scoring many source episodes; moderate compute but feasible on one GPU.

Impact.review: Uses real labelled source data to calibrate, potentially improving both AUROC and calibration.

Validity.review: Assumes calibration relationships transfer from source to unseen modalities; non-negative weights over correlated -log p terms may be unstable.

Novelty.review: Combining a target-support normal density with a cross-modality abnormal density learned on source data is not found in the related literature on generalist AD with normal and abnormal references.

Feasibility.review: PCA and Gaussian mixtures are cheap; requires collecting source abnormal patches.

Impact.review: A two-sided test could give real power gains at small K.

Validity.review: Relies on the abnormal density transferring across modalities, which is the central and untested assumption.

Novelty.review: Score normalisation for domain generalisation in anomaly detection exists (2509.10951); importing S-norm from speaker verification is a moderately new angle.

Feasibility.review: Cohort banks from source modalities are easy to build.

Clarity.review: Clear Z-norm, T-norm and S-norm definitions.

Impact.review: Could make one threshold work across modalities, a useful but narrower goal.

Validity.review: Benefit depends on cohort similarity to the target, which is not guaranteed for distant modalities.
